blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Between June 2026 and October 2026, detached houses: listings rose from 25 in June to 37 in October (+48.0%), and it took 5.6% of the city’s 357 sales over the period; condos and townhomes: listings rose from 23 in June to 31 in October (+34.8%), and it took 4.8% of the city’s 694 sales over the period.
The monthly write-ups singled out Murrayville for detached houses in October (a buyers’ best bet); condos and townhomes in June, September, October (a sellers’ best bet).

Where it sits and what to know here

items.t: Blair Recreation Centre) inside the neighbourhood.
On MLS®: Murrayville is an FVREB sub-area of the Langley board community with its own SnapStats row (below).

Where the condo stock concentrates: the 48 Avenue corridor and the streets off it — every known apartment building in stands on 48 Avenue, 49 Avenue or 221A Street, within a few blocks of the Fraser Highway core — plus a townhome band along 48A/50 Avenues.
Recreation: W.C. Blair Recreation Centre is at 22200 Fraser Hwy, Langley Twp, a Township recreation centre / community centre with pool and gym.

Township zoning and plans: Murrayville sits under the Township of Langley Zoning Bylaw No. 2500. The Murrayville Community Plan is Amendment (Murrayville Community Plan) Bylaw 1988 No. 2661 to the Langley Official Community Plan Bylaw 1979 No. 1842, adopted April 17, 1989; the consolidated plan document records the further Amendment (2025 OCP Update) Bylaw No. 6200, December 1, 2025 — OCP Bylaw No. 6200 was adopted December 1, 2025. The Township's Development Permits page confirms there are currently two designated heritage conservation areas in the Township — the Fort Langley Community Plan and the Murrayville Community Plan — each with heritage guidelines in its plan, and a Heritage Alteration Permit is required before demolition, subdivision or redevelopment in one.

Township of Langley Zoning Bylaw No. 2500 Amendment (SSMUH) Bylaw No. 6020, adopted November 18, 2024 — eligible lots (inside the Urban Containment Boundary, on both municipal water and sewer, not heritage-designated, not in a Transit-Oriented Area) may have 3 units if 280 m² or smaller, or 4 units if between 280 m² and 4,050 m²; lots larger than 4,050 m² are not eligible, and the Township has no six-unit tier. A Township secondary suite is capped at 120 m² under Zoning Bylaw s. 102, as amended.
Murrayville's attached market was Langley's fastest in September 2026. There is still no Murrayville median to quote: SnapStats publishes medians at community level only.

One complex, two addresses, two build years in print. Autumn Ridge trades under both 22015 and 22025 48 Avenue as a single strata, and its year is stated as 1995 on that sheet and 1993 in other listings — search both addresses and verify the year on the Form B, not on either web line.

The Township's own Development Permits page confirms Murrayville is one of only two designated heritage conservation areas in the Township (with Fort Langley) and that a Heritage Alteration Permit is required before demolition, subdivision or redevelopment in one.

A directory entry can misstate a townhouse complex as a small apartment building. The directory's "Murrayville — 21937 Avenue" entry states built 1990 and 22 units with apartment-style framing, while listings for the same address record a townhouse complex with unit numbers running into the 1300s.

The community plan is older than the buildings it now governs. The Murrayville Community Plan is Bylaw No. 2661, adopted April 17, 1989, as an amendment to OCP Bylaw 1979 No. 1842 — and its consolidated text now carries the 2025 OCP Update (Bylaw No. 6200, December 1, 2025) in its amendment table, so a plan citation without the amendment history is incomplete for a Murrayville lot.

SSMUH eligibility in the Township is a servicing test, not a slogan (Township SSMUH page). A Murrayville lot needs the Urban Containment Boundary, municipal water AND sewer, no heritage designation and no Transit-Oriented Area status before the 3- or 4-unit count in Bylaw 6020 is even available — test the exact lot, not the neighbourhood.
